The sources of offences include careless words or actions (James 3:2), unmet expectations (2 Timothy 4:16), pride, envy, and selfishness (3 John 9-10).
The danger of offences includes bitterness and strife (Hebrews 12:15), spiritual wavering (Matthew 24:10), and hindered prayers (Mark 11:25-26).

p.instruction: Put these sentences from How to Manage Offences in the order printed.
shuffled: Seek Peace, Pursue peace with all men, as much as lies in you (Hebrews 12:14; Romans 12:18).
Be Quick to Listen, Slow to Speak, many offences can be prevented by careful communication (James 1:19).
Other practical ways Believers can manage offences include:
Guard Your Heart, do not allow bitterness to take root (Proverbs 4:23).

The Bible outline various ways to handle offences: Personal approach, that is, speaking directly with the person, not gossip about it (Matthew 18:15); The witness approach, if unresolved, involve one or two mature believers as witnesses (Matthew 18:16); The Church approach, if still unresolved, escalate it to church leadership for intervention (Matthew 18:17); Forgiveness must be part of our lifestyle (Matthew 18:21-22; Colossians 3:13); Let love rule because it covers a multitude of sins (1 Peter 4:8); Choose reconciliation over retaliation (Romans 12:17-19).
Pray for Grace, Pray for those who offend you; ask God for strength to forgive (Philippians 4:6-7).
Avoid Being a Source of Offence, Live sensitively so others are not made to stumble (Romans 14:13; 1 Corinthians 8:9).
